question_text: What does an electric circuit mean?
answer_text: A continuous and closed path of an electric current is called an electric circuit. An electric circuit consists of electric devices, source of electricity and wires that are connected with the help of a switch.
final_answer: An electric circuit is a continuous and closed path for electric current.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the definition of an electric circuit.

subject: science
question_text: Define the unit of current.
answer_text: The unit of electric current is ampere (A). 1 A is defined as the flow of 1 C of charge through a wire in 1 s.
final_answer: The unit of current is ampere, defined as the flow of 1 coulomb of charge per second.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the definition of the unit of current.

question_text: What is meant by saying that the potential difference between two points is 1 V?
answer_text: If 1 J of work is required to move a charge of amount 1 C from one point to another, then it is said that the potential difference between the two points is 1 V.
final_answer: A potential difference of 1 V means 1 J of work is done to move 1 C of charge.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of work and charge relationship.

question_text: On what factors does the resistance of a conductor depend?
answer_text: The resistance of a conductor depends upon the following factors: Length of the conductor, Cross-sectional area of the conductor, Material of the conductor, Temperature of the conductor.
final_answer: Resistance depends on length, area, material, and temperature of the conductor.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of multiple factors affecting resistance.

subject: science
question_text: Will current flow more easily through a thick wire or a thin wire of the same material, when connected to the same source? Why?
answer_text: The current will flow more easily through thick wire. It is because the resistance of a conductor is inversely proportional to its area of cross-section.
final_answer: Thicker wires have less resistance, allowing more current to flow.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of resistance and cross-sectional area.

question_text: Why are coils of electric toasters and electric irons made of an alloy rather than a pure metal?

question_text: What are the advantages of connecting electrical devices in parallel with the battery instead of connecting them in series?
answer_text: There is no division of voltage among the appliances when connected in parallel. The potential difference across each appliance is equal to the supplied voltage. The total effective resistance of the circuit can be reduced by connecting electrical appliances in parallel.
final_answer: Thus, connecting devices in parallel ensures equal voltage and reduces total resistance.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electrical circuits and their configurations.

question_text: (a) Why is tungsten used almost exclusively for the filament of electric lamps? (b) Why are the conductors of electric heating devices, such as bread-toasters and electric irons, made of an alloy rather than a pure metal? (c) Why is the series arrangement not used for domestic circuits? (d) How does the resistance of a wire vary with its area of cross-section? (e) Why are copper and aluminium wires usually employed for electricity transmission?

mcq_options.option_text: Why is tungsten used almost exclusively for the filament of electric lamps?
Why are the conductors of electric heating devices, such as bread-toasters and electric irons, made of an alloy rather than a pure metal?
Why is the series arrangement not used for domestic circuits?
How does the resistance of a wire vary with its area of cross-section? (e) Why are copper and aluminium wires usually employed for electricity transmission?

parts.part_text: Why is tungsten used almost exclusively for the filament of electric lamps?
parts.answer_text: Tungsten has a very high melting point and high resistivity, so it does not burn easily at high temperatures.
parts.final_answer: Thus, tungsten is ideal for lamp filaments.

parts.part_text: Why are the conductors of electric heating devices, such as bread-toasters and electric irons, made of an alloy rather than a pure metal?
parts.answer_text: The resistivity of an alloy is higher than that of pure metals, which produces a larger amount of heat.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, alloys are preferred for heating devices.

parts.part_text: Why is the series arrangement not used for domestic circuits?
parts.answer_text: In series circuits, voltage is divided among components, leading to reduced current and improper functioning of devices.
parts.final_answer: Hence, series arrangements are unsuitable for domestic use.

parts.part_text: How does the resistance of a wire vary with its area of cross-section?
parts.answer_text: Resistance is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section; as the area increases, resistance decreases.
parts.final_answer: Thus, larger cross-sections result in lower resistance.

parts.part_text: Why are copper and aluminium wires usually employed for electricity transmission?
parts.answer_text: Copper and aluminium are good conductors with low resistivity, making them ideal for electricity transmission.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, they are commonly used in electrical wiring.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of multiple concepts related to electricity and materials.
